claims.text: The AWSx ELB component provides APIs for provisioning Application and Network Load Balancers and integrates with API Gateway, ECS, Lambda, and VPC.
In Pulumi AWSx, `NetworkLoadBalancer` is used for NLBs and `ApplicationLoadBalancer` is used for ALBs.
The example load balancer listens on port 80 in the account's per-region default VPC using its public subnets, exposing it to the internet.
ALBs automatically open ingress traffic to the ports they listen on, whereas NLBs do not.
Targeting an EC2 instance requires opening ingress to the load balancer (explicitly needed for NLB but not ALB); the steps are described as five steps.
The AWSx load balancer creates a default target group that forwards traffic on the same port.
The Pulumi AWS registry has API docs for ec2 LaunchTemplate at /registry/packages/aws/api-docs/ec2/launchtemplate/ and autoscaling Group at /registry/packages/aws/api-docs/autoscaling/group/.
When the load balancer's target group is passed in an ECS task definition's `portMappings`, AWSx uses that target group to populate the ECS service's load balancer configuration.
The AWSx ECS component (awsx.ecs classes) automatically creates the right ingress and egress rules; with raw aws.ecs you must manage security group rules manually.
The stack output for the ECS Fargate nginx example is named `url`, and curl of it returns the nginx page.
ECS supports both NLB and ALB, and ALBs offer two features (dynamic host port mapping; path-based routing and priority rules) that make them more attractive for ECS.
Pulumi recommends ALBs for ECS services unless a service requires a feature only available with NLBs.
By default an AWSx load balancer is created internet-facing using the VPC's public subnets; setting `internal` to true makes it private.
AWSx load balancers accept either a `subnets` property (subnet objects) or a `subnetIds` property (subnet IDs).
NLBs support listener protocols TCP, TLS, UDP, TCP_UDP, QUIC, and TCP_QUIC, while ALBs support HTTP and HTTPS; NLBs default to TCP and ALBs choose HTTP or HTTPS based on port.
AWS docs pages rule-action-types.html (fixed-response-actions, redirect-actions anchors) and listener-rules.html exist under elasticloadbalancing application docs.
The `deregistrationDelay` range is 0–3600 seconds and the default is 300.
The `slowStart` range is 30–900 seconds or 0 to disable, and it is disabled by default.
Target group `stickiness` is available for ALBs only.

The target group `targetType` values are `instance`, `ip`, `lambda`, and `alb`, default `instance`; IP targets must be within the VPC private subnet range, RFC 1918 ranges, or RFC 6598 range (100.64.0.0/10).
The health check `interval` range is 5–300 seconds and the default is 30 seconds.
The health check `healthyThreshold` range is 2–10 and the default is 3.
The health check `unhealthyThreshold` range is 2–10, default 3, and for NLBs must equal `healthyThreshold`.
The health check `timeout` range is 2–120 seconds; AWS default is 6 seconds for HTTP target groups and 10 seconds for HTTPS, TCP, and TLS target groups.
HTTP/2 is not supported for NLBs.
